proof: For the independent fair walk stopped at 0 or 6, p0=0,p6=1 and pk=(p(k-1)+p(k+1))/2. Adjacent differences are equal, uniquely giving pk=k/6. Absorption occurs almost surely: from any interior state, a block of six heads (probability 1/64 independently per block) guarantees prior absorption, so survival beyond m blocks is at most (63/64)^m. Thus the finite boundary recurrence describes eventual winning, without assuming finite simulations prove the probability.
limits: Independent calculation and source inspection; numerical checks supplement the general argument. No learning outcome inferred.
